digo_source: Pakia (2005) App. III, V, VI; Mgombato ('mwenjere')
swahili: Mwenjere (shared with Digo, Pakia App. VI); mwengele (Mgombato)

teaser.en: A climber of the grape family that Digo speakers can name by taste alone: its leaves are sour.
teaser.sw: Mtambaa wa familia ya mizabibu ambao wasemaji wa Kidigo wanaweza kuutaja kwa ladha peke yake: majani yake ni machachu.

summary.en: Mgongolo mlume, also called mwenjere, is a wild climber of the grape family with sour-tasting leaves. Its first name casts it as the 'male' of another plant, mgongolo.
summary.sw: Mgongolo mlume, unaoitwa pia *mwenjere*, ni mtambaa wa porini wa familia ya mizabibu wenye majani yenye ladha ya uchachu. Jina lake la kwanza linauweka kama 'dume' la mmea mwingine, *mgongolo*.

about.en:
*Mgongolo mlume* is a climbing or scrambling plant of the grape family. Like its relatives it holds on with coiled tendrils that grow opposite the leaves. The leaves are divided into several leaflets with toothed edges, and the young stems and leaves often carry sticky glandular hairs. Small greenish flowers grow in flat-topped clusters, and they are followed by small, juicy berries that turn red as they ripen.

Pakia notes that Digo speakers identify it by the look of the whole plant and by the taste of its leaves, which are *kakasi*, sour. It is one of the few wild plants that people recognise mainly by taste.
about.sw:
*Mgongolo mlume* ni mmea unaopanda au kutambaa wa familia ya mizabibu. Kama jamaa zake, hujishikilia kwa vikonyo vilivyojikunja vinavyoota upande wa pili wa majani. Majani yamegawanyika kuwa vijani kadhaa vyenye meno pembeni, na mashina machanga na majani mara nyingi huwa na manyoya ya tezi yanayonata. Maua madogo ya rangi ya kijani-kijani huota katika vishada vyenye vilele bapa, na hufuatwa na matunda madogo yenye maji mengi yanayogeuka mekundu yanapoiva.

Pakia anabainisha kwamba wasemaji wa Kidigo huutambua kwa sura ya mmea mzima na kwa ladha ya majani yake, ambayo ni *kakasi*, machachu. Ni mojawapo ya mimea michache ya porini ambayo watu huitambua hasa kwa ladha.

where.en: It grows over bushes and along thicket and forest edges, scrambling up into other vegetation. The species is widespread in tropical Africa and is common in the coastal bush of Kwale.
where.sw: Hukua juu ya vichaka na kando ya vichaka na pembezoni mwa misitu, ukitambaa na kupanda juu ya mimea mingine. Spishi hii imeenea katika Afrika ya tropiki na ni ya kawaida katika vichaka vya pwani vya Kwale.

culture.en: Pakia uses this plant as his example of the sour taste (*kakasi*) in Digo plant identification. Bitter (*utsungu*) and sweet (*mtswano*) are the other two taste words people use.
culture.sw: Pakia anautumia mmea huu kama mfano wake wa ladha ya uchachu (*kakasi*) katika utambuzi wa mimea kwa Kidigo. Uchungu (*utsungu*) na utamu (*mtswano*) ni maneno mengine mawili ya ladha ambayo watu huyatumia.

names.en: *Mgongolo mlume* means 'male mgongolo'. Pakia records that people see it as the male form of *mgongolo* (*Hoslundia opposita*), though he adds that neither plant has any clear link with *gongolo*, the millipede. Its other name, *mwenjere*, is shared with Swahili, and the Mgombato dictionary lists *mwenjere* as 'type of plant (Cyphostemma adenocaulis)', with Swahili *mwengele*. No English name is recorded.
names.sw: *Mgongolo mlume* maana yake ni '*mgongolo* dume'. Pakia anarekodi kwamba watu huuona kuwa umbo la kiume la *mgongolo* (*Hoslundia opposita*), ingawa anaongeza kwamba hakuna kati ya mimea hii miwili yenye uhusiano wa wazi na *gongolo*, jongoo. Jina lake jingine, *mwenjere*, linashirikiwa na Kiswahili, na kamusi ya Mgombato inaorodhesha *mwenjere* kama 'aina ya mmea (Cyphostemma adenocaulis)', kwa Kiswahili *mwengele*. Hakuna jina la Kiingereza lililorekodiwa.
